progress.description: Pipeline 4 runtime and installer work remains tracked below. Repair voice recovery now always creates TTS-ready copies, resolves book TTS from selected chunks JSON path, prioritizes JSON voice_used matches in direct TTS storage, passes selected paths directly into GUI resynthesis, emits exhaustive lookup debugging, candidate lists, path details, and resynthesis traces, and now removes hardcoded repo-root sys.path injection from src/chatterbox_vllm/tts.py.
progress.phase1_status_panel: New in-process callback mechanism (modules/progress_tracker.py: emit_phase_status/emit_final_status/_relay_status) mirrors the existing log_chunk_progress._status_callback pattern but sends already-structured dicts (no regex parsing needed). Wired in chatterbox_gui.py's ProcessThread.run() alongside the legacy callback. true_start_time added at process_book_folder entry as the Total Elapsed anchor (button press -> file actually written, measured AFTER WAV combine + M4B conversion, not before). max_attempts_spin wired into quality_params -> MAX_REGENERATION_ATTEMPTS override (was fully disconnected before). REFINED after user feedback on real behavior: (1) Current Operation is now the ONLY 'what's happening' field -- the old 'Current Phase' row was just duplicating it, so emit_phase_status no longer sets chunk_info at all; the shared 'Current Chunk:' row/label stays in the StructuredStatusPanel class unused by Tab 1 (kept only because Tab 8 still relies on it for its own unrelated per-chunk display). (2) avg_its widget/row/forwarding fully deleted (was requested removed, not just fixed). (3) Split one generic 'Phase Elapsed' into separate phase1_elapsed_label/phase2_elapsed_label, each frozen at its final value once that phase ends (no code needed for the freeze -- update_status only overwrites a label when a truthy value arrives, and nothing emits phase1_elapsed after Phase 1 ends). (4) Fixed a real dead-air bug: panel used to stay on stale 'Phase 0' text through the whole vLLM engine load + first token-generation batch of Phase 1 (no callback fires until a batch actually completes) -- now emit_phase_status(1, 'Loading T3 model...') fires immediately when Phase 1 begins, before engine construction. (5) Fixed a second dead-air bug: nothing updated between Phase 2 finishing and the final 'Processing Complete' -- now emit_phase_status(None, 'Finalizing: combining audio & converting to M4B', ...) fires right after Phase 2, before WAV combine/M4B conversion (uses phase=None so the text has no awkward 'Phase None:' prefix). (6) Realtime Factor / 'Elapsed Time' now correctly span Phase 1 start -> Phase 2 finish ONLY (excludes Phase 0's conditional-computation time) by passing phase1_start as _finalize_book_output's start_time argument for vllm/turbo-hybrid callers specifically (legacy backend's call sites unchanged). ASR-regen status display (user also asked for this) is NOT done yet -- it depends on Phase 3 existing.
progress.phase2_cfg_weight: CHATTERBOX_CFG_SCALE env var now set from tts_params['cfg_weight'] (the GUI's base value) fresh each run, before the vLLM engine loads, in both vllm and turbo-hybrid blocks. Previously nothing in the codebase ever set this env var, so every run silently used the hardcoded default 0.5 regardless of GUI setting. Per-chunk VADER variation of cfg_weight still architecturally impossible (CFG scale is a fixed attribute read once at T3VllmModel.__init__, not a per-request field) -- this fix only makes the one load-time baseline value correct, not per-chunk.
progress.verification: REAL check = faster-whisper transcription matches input text (venv HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, model 'base'). Spectral 'speech-like' stats are NOT verification. Phase 1/2 changes verified: (a) pipeline 3 and pipeline 4 smoke-test runs both completed and transcribed correctly after the changes (no regression), (b) phase-status STATUS: lines confirmed firing correctly for Phase 0/1/2 + final complete via headless fallback print, (c) cfg_weight wiring proven by re-running with cfg_weight=0.8 vs default 0.5 and confirming the printed 'Applying CFG scale:' value changed accordingly (the 0.5 case alone can't prove it works since 0.5 is also the fallback default).
progress.phase1_live_progress: User reported Phase 1 showed zero progress on real books -- vLLM's own tqdm bar advanced in the terminal (e.g. 'Processed prompts: 42%|... 130/306...') but nothing reached the GUI. Root cause: VllmBatchProcessor groups chunks by identical TTS params into ONE vLLM .generate() call per group; that call is synchronous and our progress_callback only fired after the ENTIRE group finished, so a large single-group book (all 306 prompts in one call) looked frozen the whole time. Fix: vLLM's LLM.generate(use_tqdm=...) accepts a tqdm-compatible callable and calls .update(n) on it after every individual completed request (vllm/entrypoints/llm.py:_run_engine) -- real per-request granularity, not an approximation. Added modules/vllm_batch_processor.py:_ProgressRelay, a small tqdm-compatible shim relaying those real updates to progress_callback (throttled to >=0.2s between GUI emits, always firing on the first and last update). Discovered along the way that vLLM ALSO uses use_tqdm at a second, differently-shaped call site (LLM._validate_and_add_requests: `tqdm_func(iterable, desc=...)`, a plain iterable-wrapping usage for its 'Adding requests' bookkeeping step, unrelated to generation progress) -- _ProgressRelay.__init__ accepts an optional positional `iterable` and implements __iter__ as a transparent passthrough with no progress relay for that call site, only the total=-based _run_engine call site drives on_update. Also: src/chatterbox_vllm/tts.py's generate_speech_tokens() now has an explicit use_tqdm passthrough param (previously silently swallowed into **kwargs bound for SamplingParams, so it was always the vLLM-default True regardless of caller intent). Progress is now reported in SEGMENTS (parse_pause_tags output), computed once per chunk during chunk_metadata construction instead of recomputed per-batch -- segments==chunks in the common case (no inline pause tags yet, that's Phase 4), so this doesn't look different for typical books today. Verified on an 80-sentence single-param-group test book (all 80 in one vLLM call): live ticks observed climbing through Phase 1 (1/80 -> 15 -> 32 -> ... -> 80/80) on both pipeline 3 and pipeline 4, transcription unaffected (no regression). FOLLOW-UP BUG (2026-07-08): this fix silently killed terminal visibility for Phase 1 -- replacing vLLM's use_tqdm with _ProgressRelay meant vLLM's own terminal bar stopped printing, and _ProgressRelay.update() only relayed to the GUI callback, never printed anything itself. User correctly flagged that fixing the GUI should never have cost terminal output. Fixed: update() now always does `print(f'[T3] Phase 1: {current}/{total} tokens generated')` on every throttled tick regardless of whether a GUI callback is attached (removed the early `if not self._on_update: return` guard that would have skipped the print too when no GUI was listening). Verified on the 80-sentence test book: terminal shows climbing '[T3] Phase 1: N/80 tokens generated' lines throughout Phase 1 again, transcription still correct. FORMAT FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-08): user asked why the print format was simplified vs the original vLLM bar (percentage, ASCII bar, it/s, est. speed input/output toks/s) -- honest answer was no real reason, just wrote the minimum line. Restored full stats except the ASCII bar graphic (tqdm's own rendering, no data available to reproduce it): percentage and it/s computed locally in update() (pct = current/total*100, rate = self.n/elapsed-since-relay-start); token throughput recovered for free because vLLM itself sets self.postfix = 'est. speed input: X toks/s, output: Y toks/s' immediately before calling update() (see _run_engine) -- _ProgressRelay already stored postfix, just wasn't printing it. New format: '[T3] Phase 1: 65% | 130/306 | 22.1 it/s | est. speed input: 1321.56 toks/s, output: 2083.98 toks/s'. Verified on 80-sentence test book, transcription unaffected.
progress.group2_phase456: Implemented and verified together (Phase 4 inline pauses incl. ~1/~2 markers, Phase 5 endpoint trim, Phase 6 contextual boundary silence) since they share one code path with a strict ordering dependency. modules/pause_utils.py: new convert_inline_markers_to_pause_tags() ports the ~1/~2 shorthand from the sibling Turbo project, adapted to this repo's [pause:Xms] (integer ms) tag format instead of that project's [pause:Xs] seconds format; wired into modules/tts_engine.py's generate_enriched_chunks() chunk loop, right before the existing ENABLE_PUNCTUATION_PAUSES/add_pause_tags_to_text call, gated by config.ENABLE_INLINE_PAUSES (already existed, never had any code scanning for the literal markers before now). modules/vllm_batch_processor.py: parse_pause_tags() is called once per chunk during chunk_metadata construction (already true from the Phase-1-progress work) and now ALSO keeps pauses (previously discarded as _pauses) -- both chunk_metadata and the chunks_data return value (chunks_tokens.json) carry a 'pauses' field per chunk alongside 'speech_tokens'. modules/vllm_decoder.py's decode_tokens() gained a chunk_meta: Dict[chunk_id, {pauses, boundary_type}] param (built by a new small helper, modules/tts_engine.py:_build_chunk_meta(), from process_chunks's second return value which both vllm/turbo-hybrid blocks previously discarded as `_`) and now assembles each chunk's audio in the corrected order: (1) trim_audio_endpoint() on each RAW segment immediately after S3Gen decode, gated on config.ENABLE_AUDIO_TRIMMING -- before any deliberate silence exists to accidentally strip -- (2) concatenate trimmed segments with AudioSegment.silent() inserted between them per that chunk's pauses list, (3) once the full chunk is assembled, add_contextual_silence_memory() appends the boundary-type-specific trailing gap (chapter/paragraph/punctuation, existing config SILENCE_* values) exactly once at the very end. Note: used native pydub AudioSegment operations throughout (matching what decode_tokens already worked in) rather than pause_utils.py's torch-tensor-based insert_pauses_into_audio_tensor helper named in the original plan -- simpler, avoids an unnecessary tensor round-trip, decode_tokens never touches torch tensors after _tensor_to_audio_segment. chunk_meta param defaults to None (debug_diagnostics.py's older 2-positional-arg call site still works unchanged, verified by rerunning it). Verification: built a test book combining ~1/~2 markers, an explicit [pause:Xms] tag, and multiple paragraphs; confirmed via chunks_tokens.json that pauses/boundary_type attach correctly; confirmed via faster-whisper word-level timestamps (not fragile amplitude-threshold silence detection) that real audible gaps (0.28-0.94s) land exactly at the three pause-tag text positions and nowhere else in the transcript, on BOTH pipeline 3 and pipeline 4; confirmed ~1.0-1.3s trailing silence on every chunk matching SILENCE_PARAGRAPH_END. All test artifacts cleaned up afterward. FOLLOW-UP: user asked whether this would be visible in the terminal on real runs, or just taken on faith -- answer was no, none of it logged anything (add_contextual_silence_memory has zero logging, trim_audio_endpoint only logs at debug level on the VAD path). Added an always-on per-chunk debug line in decode_tokens (e.g. '[chunk_00000] trim=-0ms | pauses=[150, 400]ms | boundary=paragraph_end(+1000ms)'), both logger.info and print so it shows in terminal and log file. User noted this could be gated behind a future config debug checkbox or commented out later if too noisy for large books -- deferred, not needed now. Verified the line prints correctly with real pause/boundary values on a fresh test run.
progress.phase3_asr_regen: ASR + regeneration + full quality-validation cluster, implemented and verified 2026-07-09 -- the last item on the master plan. modules/vllm_decoder.py: extracted decode_and_assemble_chunk() (the trim/pause/boundary-silence assembly logic) out of decode_tokens's loop into its own reusable method, so both the main Phase 2 loop and Phase 3 regeneration attempts always assemble audio identically. decode_tokens gained asr_client/asr_threshold/enable_quality_scoring params: after each chunk's audio is finalized it (a) computes a local composite score via audio_processor.evaluate_chunk_quality(combined, reference_text=None, ...) -- reference_text=None deliberately, so it never triggers that function's own synchronous non-daemon ASR path -- and (b) if given an asr_client, submits the chunk WAV to it non-blocking (decode continues immediately to the next chunk; this IS the concurrency the user asked for). decode_tokens's return signature changed from (generated, skipped) to (generated, skipped, local_scores); debug_diagnostics.py's older call site doesn't unpack the return so is unaffected, both tts_engine.py call sites updated. New module modules/regeneration_engine.py: compute_composite_score(local_score, asr_result) averages an already-computed local float score with the async ASR daemon's score (never re-scores audio, since decode_tokens already did that once); regenerate_failed_chunks() reloads the T3-only vLLM engine ONCE for ALL failed chunks' retries (not per-chunk), then reloads the decoder ONCE for ALL attempts' decode -- matching the existing 'never load T3 and S3Gen simultaneously' phase-safety design used everywhere else in this pipeline. Ported from /home/danno/MyApps/Turbo/modules/regeneration_engine.py: generates config.MAX_REGENERATION_ATTEMPTS retries per failed chunk (progressive temperature/exaggeration reduction via config.REGEN_TEMPERATURE_ADJUSTMENT/REGEN_EXAGGERATION_ADJUSTMENT, cfg_weight deliberately left untouched since it can't vary within one loaded engine per the Phase 2 cfg_weight fix), decodes+submits every attempt to ASR non-blocking before scoring any of them (so earlier attempts' ASR results are likely already back by the time the last attempt finishes decoding), picks the max-scoring attempt INCLUDING the original, moves losing attempts to a Failed/ subfolder, writes asr_regeneration_report.json/asr_remaining_failures.json. tts_engine.py: _build_chunk_meta extended to carry text/tts_params/segments (not just pauses/boundary_type) so a failed chunk can be regenerated without re-reading chunks_info.json; new _maybe_start_asr_daemon() (starts ASR/asr_daemon.py's ASRDaemonClient BEFORE Phase 2 decode begins, gated on ENABLE_REGENERATION_LOOP AND enable_asr) and _run_phase3_regen() (collects ASR results after Phase 2, computes composite scores, builds the failed-chunks list, calls regenerate_failed_chunks, shuts down the daemon) shared by both vllm and turbo-hybrid blocks to avoid duplicating ~80 lines twice. ASR quality tier wiring: ASR/asr_daemon.py gained a --model-size CLI arg (was hardcoded 'base'), threaded through tools/asr_client.py's ASRDaemonClient; new _resolve_asr_model_size() reuses the GUI's own existing modules/system_detector.get_system_profile()/recommend_asr_models() (previously only used for the SAFE/MODERATE/INSANE preview text, never actually affecting anything) so the daemon's real model matches what the GUI told the user it would use; chatterbox_gui.py's start_standard_conversion now actually captures asr_level (previously only read inside the cosmetic update_asr_models preview method) and passes it through process_book_folder's new asr_level param. TWO BUGS found and fixed during verification, both real: (1) regeneration_engine.py's `from config.config import MAX_REGENERATION_ATTEMPTS` captured the static config.py default (3) at import time and never saw quality_params's GUI override that tts_engine.py's own copy of the global correctly receives -- fixed by having _run_phase3_regen pass max_attempts=MAX_REGENERATION_ATTEMPTS (tts_engine.py's own live copy) explicitly into regenerate_failed_chunks rather than relying on regeneration_engine.py's stale import. (2) evaluate_chunk_quality's sub-scores can be numpy.float32, which crashed json.dumps when writing the regeneration report -- fixed by casting compute_composite_score's return to float() explicitly. Verification: built a small test book, ran twice per pipeline -- once with a lenient threshold (confirmed ASR daemon starts with the correct model tier, scores both chunks, 0 regenerations triggered, clean daemon shutdown with empty queue/results dirs afterward, transcription correct) and once with an artificially impossible 0.99 threshold to force every chunk through the full regeneration path (confirmed T3+decoder reload, correct attempt count matching the GUI's max_attempts override, composite scoring, max-selection picking the best attempt even when none clear the bar, Failed/ folder correctly populated with the displaced originals, valid JSON reports, and the final shipped (regenerated) audio transcribes correctly) -- on BOTH pipeline 3 and pipeline 4. All test artifacts cleaned up afterward; no stray ASR daemon processes left running.

decisions.unified_venv: All deps in main venv (vllm==0.10.0, faster-whisper, peft, etc.). No separate vLLM or ASR venvs. VERIFIED WORKING.
decisions.model_internals_frozen: src/chatterbox_vllm/models/ must stay byte-identical to the proven Dec 23 snapshot. Never hack model attention/CFG internals again; the 'flash attention assert' saga was self-inflicted, not stock vLLM behavior.
decisions.vllm_engine_config: V1 engine, in-process: VLLM_USE_V1=1 + VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0, set inside from_local() before LLM(). Required because TokenizerRegistry/ModelRegistry registrations are in-process dicts invisible to the default EngineCore subprocess. VLLM_USE_V1=0 is NOT the verified config.
decisions.vllm_model_dir: from_local() picks the first model dir with config.json and exactly ONE *.safetensors: config VLLM_*_CKPT_DIR override -> chatterbox-vllm/t3-model -> ./t3-model. Top-level ./t3-model is polluted with s3gen/ve/t3_cfg safetensors which vLLM would load as shards and crash on.
decisions.load_t3_only: ChatterboxTTS.from_local() gets load_t3_only param. Saves ~0.5GB VRAM during Phase 1.
decisions.vllm_decoder: Unified class with 'standard' and 'turbo' decoder_type. One new case per future decoder.
decisions.asr_ipc: ASR daemon file-based IPC (ASR/asr_daemon.py + tools/asr_client.py) now wired into Phase 3 (2026-07-09): started before Phase 2 decode, chunks submitted non-blocking as each is written, results collected after Phase 2 finishes. Confirmed working via sys.executable (main venv) in verification runs -- daemon starts, scores, and shuts down cleanly with empty queue/results dirs afterward.
decisions.pipelines_3_4_same: Pipelines 3 (vllm) and 4 (turbo-hybrid) differ only by decoder_type param.
decisions.chunk_id_zero: chunk_id/index 0 is valid; never use `or`/`not` truthiness on chunk ids (fixed in vllm_batch_processor.py 2026-07-08).
decisions.cfg_weight_per_chunk_impossible: CFG scale can only be set once per vLLM engine load (T3VllmModel reads CHATTERBOX_CFG_SCALE env var in __init__, applies it as a fixed attribute in compute_logits for every request). VADER's per-chunk cfg_weight suggestion is computed/stored in JSON but cannot take effect per-chunk without a full engine reload per unique value -- not planned, would defeat the batch pipeline's purpose.
decisions.decode_progress_callback_shape: VllmDecoder.decode_tokens's progress_callback signature changed from (pct, message) to (current, total, message) -- both vllm and turbo-hybrid blocks in tts_engine.py updated to match.
decisions.process_chunks_signature: VllmBatchProcessor.process_chunks dropped dead total_chunks/start_time params (never used), added progress_callback: Callable[[int,int],None] called after each param-group batch completes.
decisions.pipeline4_dependency_audit_20260722: Verified live Pipeline 4 imports src/chatterbox_vllm (not the nonexistent chatterbox-vllm/src/chatterbox_vllm). Phase 0 needs t3_cfg.safetensors, ve.safetensors, s3gen.safetensors, and conds.pt; Phase 1 reuses that one t3_cfg checkpoint through chatterbox-vllm/t3-model/model.safetensors symlink; Phase 2 needs Turbo s3gen_meanflow.safetensors only. Turbo t3_turbo_v1.safetensors and src/chatterbox_turbo/models/t3 are unused. Current tts_engine pre-branch punc_norm import and VllmDecoder Turbo VoiceEncoder construction are removable legacy/no-op dependencies, but the unmodified monolith still imports them. Offline target must set TURBO_CKPT_DIR explicitly and bundle/cache Silero VAD or disable default USE_VAD_FOR_TRIMMING.
